ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: It is known that the point $(-3,-1)$ and the point $(4,-6)$ are on two sides of the line $3 x-2 y-a=0$, then the range of values of $a$ is ( )
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The problem gives two points P=(-3,-1), Q=(4,-6), and the line is 3x-2y-a=0. Let the line expression be F(x,y)=3x-2y-a. Substituting P gives F(P)=3(-3)-2(-1)-a=-9+2-a=-7-a. Substituting Q gives F(Q)=3(4)-2(-6)-a=12+12-a=24-a. When two points are on opposite sides of the line, the signs obtained by substituting into the line expression are opposite, so F(P)F(Q)<0, that is (-7-a)(24-a)<0. Simplifying gives (a+7)(a-24)<0, therefore a is between the two roots, obtaining -7<a<24.
